note: Conformance vectors for ASTM F3411 / Open Drone ID message decoding. Each case is a 25-byte message in hex and the fields a decoder should produce from it. Intended for checking a second implementation — an ESP32 in C, or your own tracker — against the same cases the Python decoder is checked against. Absent values are the string "N/A"; an empty expect object means the message carries no usable data.

cases.name: height and geodetic altitude are both present
cases.why: An aircraft broadcasts both. Reporting one and discarding the other loses the number that answers the other question.

cases.name: height type flag says above ground
cases.why: Bit 2 of byte 1 separates above-takeoff from above-ground, and the two differ by the whole climb of a launch from a rooftop.

cases.name: no height broadcast, geodetic only
cases.why: Wing and Zipline send the no-value sentinel for height on moving aircraft. Substituting absolute altitude silently made them look like they cruise hundreds of feet higher than everyone else.

cases.name: barometric altitude only
cases.why: Falls back to barometric when geodetic is absent, and still calls it absolute rather than implying it is height above ground.

cases.name: no altitude of any kind
cases.why: A position with no vertical information must not report a made-up one.

cases.name: below sea level is a real altitude
cases.why: Death Valley and the Dead Sea exist. A negative geodetic altitude is data, not an error.

cases.name: westerly heading adds 180 degrees
cases.why: Direction is stored in one byte, so the east/west bit carries the other half of the circle.

cases.name: the speed multiplier changes the scale
cases.why: Above 63.75 m/s the encoding switches scale. Ignoring the bit understates a fast aircraft by a factor that grows with its speed.

cases.name: descending aircraft has negative vertical speed
cases.why: Vertical speed is signed. Reading it unsigned turns a descent into a climb of about 64 m/s.

cases.name: null island is the no-position sentinel
cases.why: 0,0 means the aircraft has no position fix, not that it is in the Atlantic. Plotting it puts phantom aircraft off the coast of Africa.

cases.name: southern and western hemispheres
cases.why: Coordinates are signed 32-bit. Reading them unsigned puts an aircraft on the wrong side of the planet.

cases.name: basic id carries the serial and airframe class
cases.why: This is the only message that says which aircraft the rest belongs to.

cases.name: basic id with no serial
cases.why: An all-zero id field is absent, not an empty-string aircraft.

cases.name: system message locates the operator
cases.why: The operator position is a different thing from the aircraft position, and the location type says what it actually means.

cases.name: system message with no operator position
cases.why: Same 0,0 sentinel as the aircraft position. A delivery drone flying from a nest reports this often.
